clue.text: Perturb the workers, but conclude a deal

parts.note: to perturb someone is to shake them up
hands are manual workers, as in farmhands

explanation.surface: A boss unsettles the staff yet still closes a business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Two parties clasp palms to seal an agreement, so the gesture stands for settling a bargain.

clue.text: Big bag of plunder

explanation.definitionFit: A large coarse bag for coal or flour; also the pillaging of a captured town.

clue.text: Among men, a remarkable Greek leader

indicators.note: remarkable hints the letters can be remarked, set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A notable Greek commander stands out among his men.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the king of Mycenae who led the Greek host against Troy in Homer.

clue.text: Regret having taken head off bird

indicators.note: taking the head off means the opening letter of the word regret is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry to have beheaded a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white wading heron.

clue.text: Club found in weapon store

explanation.definitionFit: A North London football club takes its name from the armoury at Woolwich, a store for guns.

clue.text: Ran and just made the five ten

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted and only just managed to turn five into ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubled back means ran, and multiplying five by two gives ten.

clue.text: Pert female comes with insolence

parts.note: lip is slang for cheeky backchat or insolence

explanation.surface: A cheeky woman arrives full of sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip is an informal adjective for flippant or saucy, a near synonym of cheeky.

clue.text: Notice nothing's turned up for her

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the whole sequence reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Nobody has paid any attention to her advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reverses AD + NIL, giving the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a woman's first name, so it can stand for 'her'.

clue.text: New stamps sure to receive approval

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into something fresh by rearranging

explanation.surface: Fresh postage stamps are certain to be accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be good enough to be accepted is the idiom for meeting the required standard.

clue.text: Beautiful singing could be noble act

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form another phrase when rearranged

explanation.surface: Fine vocals might count as a gracious deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel canto, Italian for fine song, is the lyrical operatic style of vocal performance.

clue.text: Seat one gets into daily

indicators.note: gets into tells us the numeral goes inside the word for the cleaner

parts.note: a daily or char is a British term for a cleaning lady who comes in each day
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone squeezes onto a bench on the morning commute with their daily paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' suggests a newspaper, but here it is the British cleaning lady, a CHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a piece of furniture made for sitting on.

clue.text: French wine enters USA to be drunk

indicators.note: being drunk means the letters of the two words stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A French wine is imported into America to be consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region.

clue.text: Submitted to the Spanish Guard

parts.note: to send in an application is to submit it
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders to Spanish soldiers on watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier posted to keep watch, a sentry.

clue.text: Magic spell is about to do damage

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
to harm is to do damage

explanation.surface: A witch's incantation is about to cause havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm is an incantation thought to have magical power.

clue.text: Good demonstration of being impervious to noise?

parts.note: sound means reliable or good, as in sound advice
a proof is a demonstration that something is true

explanation.surface: A fine example of resisting din.
explanation.definitionFit: A room built to block noise keeps out all external sound.

clue.text: Admit objective is a bad mistake

parts.note: to own up is to admit, so own means admit
a goal is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: Confessing one's aim turns out to be a serious blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring against your own side is football's image for any self-inflicted blunder.

clue.text: How to take a kangaroo unawares?

definitions.text: How to take a kangaroo unawares?

parts.words: How to take a kangaroo unawares?
parts.note: an idiom for catching someone off guard, applied to a bounding animal caught mid-bounce

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about surprising an Australian marsupial.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching someone unprepared is the idiom, and a kangaroo moves by jumping.

clue.text: Enticingly shows daughter to old tribesmen

parts.note: the Angles were a Germanic tribe who settled in early England

explanation.surface: A father parades his daughter before elders of a tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle something is to hold it out as a temptation, like a carrot before a donkey.

clue.text: Handled glasses

parts.note: not drinking vessels that have been touched but spectacles fitted with a long handle

explanation.surface: Tumblers that someone has picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held to the eyes by a long handle.

clue.text: Always going express

explanation.definitionFit: Something constantly moving runs without a break, and an express train makes no stops between termini.

clue.text: Take part in show, having informal agreement to include amateur

indicators.note: to include means the amateur word sits inside the agreement word

parts.note: a pact is an agreement or deal
lay means non-professional, as in a lay preacher

explanation.surface: A performer joins a production under a casual deal that allows amateurs.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend or perform theatrically is to put on an act.

clue.text: Whip firm into sudden spurt

indicators.note: into says the firm's abbreviation is placed inside the spurt

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rush or spurt
CO, short for company, is a firm

explanation.surface: A rider uses the crop firmly to make the horse put on a burst of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip used for flogging.

clue.text: Tell me how much you need for a drink

definitions.text: Tell me how much you need for a drink

parts.words: Tell me how much you need for a drink
parts.note: a host pouring a drink invites the guest to call a stop at the right amount

explanation.surface: A bartender asks how big a measure the customer wants.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what someone pouring asks so the guest can signal when to stop.

clue.text: The snow-line?

parts.note: not the altitude where snow lies year-round but a marked track down the snow for skiers

explanation.surface: A geography question about where the snow starts on a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a prepared ski run, literally a line or trail on the snow.

clue.text: Starts to see urgent truths, reading an Eastern scripture

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A guide to pressing truths found by studying an Oriental text.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutra is a Hindu or Buddhist aphorism or collection of teachings.

clue.text: No special item selected from many thin garments

indicators.note: selected from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shopper picks no particular piece from a rack of flimsy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying any old thing will do means no particular object is preferred.

clue.text: A certain time with one voluptuous charmer

parts.note: an hour is a fixed period of time
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An appointment with a seductive temptress.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition houris are beautiful maidens of paradise, hence any alluring woman.

clue.text: Girl keeping pupil in

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl gives a student detention.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a woman's name, and the coloured ring of the eye surrounds the pupil.

clue.text: As a professional he may be painfully manipulative

definitions.text: As a professional he may be painfully manipulative

parts.words: As a professional he may be painfully manipulative
parts.note: reads like a cruel schemer, but describes a practitioner whose job is manipulating bones and joints, sometimes uncomfortably

explanation.surface: A warning about a scheming career man who causes hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: This practitioner treats ailments by physically manipulating the spine and joints.

clue.text: Pronounce complete

explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce words is to speak them aloud; as an adjective the word means total, as in sheer nonsense.

clue.text: Loophole in strong regulation

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical direction meaning loud or strong
a law is a rule or regulation

explanation.surface: Someone spots a gap in a tough new rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a weakness or defect in a set of rules, a fault in their drafting.

clue.text: Lack of generosity gave sharp pain to one head

parts.note: a sting is a sharp smarting pain
I is the Roman numeral for one
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names

explanation.surface: Being mean caused a sharp ache in somebody's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanness with money is the opposite of open-handed generosity.
